memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Jacob blessed Pharaoh and went out from his presence. So Joseph settled his father and his brothers in Egypt and gave them property in the best part of the land, the district of Rameses, as Pharaoh directed. Joseph also provided his father and his brothers and all his father's household with food, according to the number of their children." — Gen 47:10-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"According to the number of their children." What a detail. Joseph does not hand out a standard ration to each household and call it fair. He gives according to actual need — a family with eight children receives more than a family with two.

That is not favouritism. That is genuine care. Real provision pays attention to circumstances rather than applying a formula.

And this is happening in the middle of the worst famine in living memory. All around them Egypt is starving, and this family is being fed carefully, individually, name by name.

God's care for His people works the same way. He is not distributing a standard allowance from a distance. Jesus said your Father knows what you need before you ask Him (Matt 6:8), and He knows it specifically — your circumstances, your household, your particular pressure.

Notice too where the provision comes from: a brother they had wronged, now positioned to sustain them. They eat every day because of a man they once tried to be rid of.

We live daily on the provision of One we had rejected. That is the gospel in a sentence.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe God's care for you is general, or specific to your situation?
2. Where do you need to trust Him with a particular need this week?
3. Do you give to others by formula, or with attention to their actual circumstances?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You know exactly what I need and care about the particulars of my life. Help me trust You, and to care for others with the same attention. Amen.
